/-!
# Erdős Problem 982

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/982](https://www.erdosproblems.com/982)
-/

open EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos982

/--
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then some vertex has at least
$\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ different distances to other vertices.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_982 (n : ℕ) (hn : 3 ≤ n) (p : Fin n → ℝ²) (hp : Function.Injective p)
    (hp' : EuclideanGeometry.IsConvexPolygon p) :
    ∃ (i : Fin n), { d : ℝ | ∃ j : Fin n, j ≠ i ∧ d = dist (p i) (p j) }.ncard ≥ n / 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos982

reformulations.difference: The source describes an unordered set of vertices in convex position; Lean uses an injective tuple already in cyclic boundary order, with convexity encoded by signs of all increasing triples.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every finite set in strict convex position has a cyclic boundary enumeration. Conversely, the common strict orientation of all increasing triples places every other vertex on the same side of each cyclic edge, making the tuple the boundary of its convex hull. The disjunction in IsConvexPolygon permits either orientation: i ↦ -i reverses cyclic traversal. Relabeling preserves each vertex’s distance set and hence the conclusion. The primary paper explicitly excludes collinear triples from convex position. The scratch file proves permutation invariance and the equivalence between assuming a cyclic labeling and assuming one exists; the full geometric characterization was checked mathematically, not proved in Lean.

review.notes:
The single theorem matches the cited conjecture. The distance set is finite, so Set.ncard’s infinite-set default is unreachable. Injectivity and j ≠ i exclude zero distances, and natural-number division gives the required floor. Scratch checks establish finiteness, positive distances, relabeling invariance, the n = 3 conclusion, a nonvacuous triangle instance, and two distinct distances from a square vertex. All three scratch files compile without sorry or diagnostics.

Live erdosproblems.com requests were blocked by Cloudflare. The July 9, 2026 archive records the problem as FALSIFIABLE (open); the currently accessible Erdős database agrees. No mathematical declaration remains unsettled. The reviewed file was not modified.
